einzeiler: Mail-in voting battles, Pentagon chaos and Missouri's redistricting fight
kurzfassung: State attorneys general are fighting executive efforts to restrict mail-in ballots as deadlines approach. Former National Security Advisor John Bolton weighs in on military leadership and foreign policy. Meanwhile, local courts and officials address high-profile legal cases and voting access disputes.
stichpunkte: State attorneys general fight executive attempts to restrict mail-in voting
Colorado and Minnesota officials emphasize secure, established local voting systems
John Bolton criticizes the administration's lack of strategy regarding Iran
The murder trial of Lindsay Clancy faces a potential mistrial after jury deadlock
The Missouri Supreme Court strikes down a redrawn Republican congressional map
Lawmakers address public incidents of white supremacist hate speech in Florida

clips.text: The frequency of voting fraud in Colorado is described as extremely minuscule, with local authorities actively prosecuting individuals who attempt to vote incorrectly across multiple properties.

clips.hook: Disputing the official narrative after an immigration shooting
clips.text: Security camera footage contradicted an initial federal report claiming a wounded individual had attacked an officer during a controversial domestic encounter.

clips.hook: Official military doctrine on civilian casualties
clips.text: United States military doctrine strictly prohibits targeting civilians in combat, though officials acknowledge that unintended casualties unfortunately occur.
State guidelines restrict how many times judges can instruct deadlocked juries to continue working toward a unanimous verdict.
Candidates are legally permitted to run for office in districts where they do not personally reside, though local voters often view the practice unfavorably.

beschreibung:
Peter Alexander interviews state Attorneys General from Colorado and Minnesota during their fight to preserve voting-by-mail for their constituents. Plus, John Bolton discusses the drama at the Defense Department and what comes next for the President. Also, Congressman Emanuel Cleaver reacts to his state supreme court tossing gerrymandered Missouri election maps.
